qt: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:

The European Court of Auditors has strongly criticised the EU’s COVID-19 recovery fund – officially the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) – in several audit reports. The European Court of Auditors’ criticisms can be summarised as follows: a lack of transparency in the use of funds, lack of monitoring of actual results, weak control and audit systems, risk of double funding, insufficient performance indicators and at times unambitious targets, as well as delays in implementation and inadequate performance monitoring and cost-effectiveness audits. The total funding amounted to a staggering EUR 573 billion , of which around EUR 450 billion has already been disbursed. In June 2026, the Austrian Ministry of Finance reported that a total of EUR 3.3305 billion had already been received from the RRF. The total allocated to Austria amounted to EUR 3.961 billion. According to earlier reports, EUR 891 million of this was channelled into the expansion of digital broadband and EUR 543 million into the Koralm railway line. Additional funding was provided for climate protection and renewable energy, as well as for primary health care centres (PHCs). As a result, Austria is to be ‘paved over’ with an ever-increasing number of wind turbines and solar parks. 1.
Which projects in Austria have received and are receiving RRF funding (full list)?
Why did the EU not monitor the appropriate and lawful use of the funding granted for these projects?
Why was the usefulness of the projects funded not examined by the EU?
